name: Safe zones in the proximal humerus
aliases: proximal humeral pin and plate safe zones
corridor: Lateral trans-deltoid pin and plate corridors that avoid the axillary nerve zone below the humeral head and the circumflex vessels, with controlled far-cortex penetration

positioning.text: Position beach-chair or supine with fluoroscopy to localize pin and plate positions relative to the humeral head.

surface_landmarks.text: Reference the top of the humeral head and the lateral acromion to estimate the axillary nerve zone.

incision.text: Use small lateral stab incisions through the deltoid for percutaneous pins.

superficial_interval.text: Insert pins laterally through the deltoid, keeping clear of the axillary nerve zone that lies about 5 to 9.5 cm below the top of the humeral head.

deep_interval.text: Let pin tips just perforate the far cortex, controlling posteromedial penetration to avoid the main axillary nerve trunk, and do not pin the long head of biceps to bone.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, deltoid, the subdeltoid space with the axillary nerve and circumflex vessels, and the proximal humeral cortex.

structures_at_risk.text: The axillary nerve below the humeral head, the anterior and posterior circumflex humeral arteries and the arcuate branch to the head, and the long head of biceps are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The band 4.5 to 9.5 cm below the top of the humeral head is the danger zone for the axillary nerve, and deep posteromedial drilling endangers its main trunk.

retraction_hazards.text: Keep far-cortex penetration minimal, especially posteromedially, and avoid transfixing the biceps tendon.

exposure.text: Defines safe lateral corridors for pins and plates rather than a formal open exposure.

limitations.text: The stated distances are guides only because axillary nerve position varies considerably, so imaging and caution remain essential.

indications.text: Indicated to guide safe pin, screw, and plate placement in the proximal humerus.

closure.text: Close each stab incision loosely around the pins.

complications.text: Complications include axillary nerve injury, circumflex vessel injury with head devascularization, and biceps tendon transfixion.

procedure_applications.condition: Percutaneous pins or a lateral plate are placed in the proximal humerus

questions.question: How far below the humeral head top does the axillary nerve risk zone lie?
questions.answer: About 4.5 to 9.5 cm below the top of the humeral head.

questions.question: How deep should pin tips go in the humeral shaft?
questions.answer: Just perforating the far cortex, with controlled posteromedial penetration.

questions.question: What structure should never be pinned to bone here?
questions.answer: The tendon of the long head of biceps.
